verdict: 2026-07-23 07:09 PDT — The overall precheck-plus-catch design is appropriate and uses existing React and adapter primitives, but the proposed mutation order retains a failure-state inconsistency and lacks a clean test seam compatible with this repository’s dependency and testing conventions.

findings.title: Failed SDK start can still mutate session and recovery state
findings.claim: The sketch still performs `sessionActions.start()` and writes `lastVideoOnRef.current = true` before awaiting `startCameraOverlay()`. A camera can turn off between the precheck and SDK call, or the SDK can reject for another reason. The catch then leaves `overlayOn` false but retains the two mutations identified by the story as incoherent. The precheck narrows the bug without making the operation transactional.
findings.alternative: Treat the SDK call as the commit boundary: probe first, await `startCameraOverlay()`, and only after it succeeds auto-start the idle session, seed `lastVideoOnRef`, set `overlayOn`, push the snapshot, and clear the notice. If preserving the existing pre-SDK session-start order is mandatory, capture and restore every affected value in the catch, though that is more complex.
findings.win: Eliminates the camera-state race and the generic-rejection partial state, with no dependency or rollback path; every refused start leaves session, overlay, and recovery baseline unchanged.

findings.title: The sketch does not provide a viable App-level unit-test seam
findings.claim: The required tests must invoke the hooked `App` callback and observe session, overlay, ref, and notice transitions, but the repository has no DOM test environment or React testing library. Existing tests deliberately extract behavior into plain functions because Vitest runs in Node. Adding jsdom/testing-library would touch manifests outside AC7, while mocking React hooks would create a brittle hand-rolled renderer.
findings.alternative: Extract the start-attempt orchestration as an exported async function in `App.jsx` with injected adapter, current status, mutation callbacks, posting, and logging; keep the hook callback as a thin adapter and test the function directly. Test `PresenterControls` notice markup using the repository’s existing direct element-tree inspection convention.
findings.win: Satisfies the behavioral assertions without new dependencies or out-of-scope files, avoids hook-mocking machinery, and centralizes the no-partial-mutation invariant in one directly testable command.
